title: A Multi-Resolvent Hierarchy for the ETH Smooth Function
abstract: The eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH) provides a statistical description of thermalization in isolated quantum many-body systems, yet the phenomenological smooth function $f_O(\bar{E},ω)$ -- which controls the energy dependence of off-diagonal matrix elements -- lacks a systematic microscopic foundation. We develop a multi-resolvent hierarchy for the correlation corrections entering the ETH smooth function. Using recursive projection identities together with a diagonal closure approximation (DCA), the hierarchy organizes multi-channel interference processes by the number of interacting bath channels, replacing the uncontrolled neglect of higher-order correlations with a systematically improvable expansion. The ETH smooth function is thereby obtained as $f_{ji}^2 = D_{ji} + \sum_{r\ge 2} g_{ji}^{(r)}$, where the diagonal baseline $D_{ji}$ and each correlation level $g_{ji}^{(r)}$ are expressed entirely through diagonal spectral functions and microscopic interaction couplings, providing a unified, closed, and systematically improvable microscopic theory. A rigorous projector sum rule constrains the entire hierarchy: the integrated off-diagonal correlation carries a negative bias of order unity, a consequence of projector idempotency. The hierarchy further reveals a parity structure in which even-$r$ sectors carry even parity under $ω\to-ω$ while the $r=3$ sector generates the first odd-parity (skewness) contribution -- absent from all single-resolvent closures -- suggesting experimentally testable signatures in quantum many-body systems.
summary: This paper introduces a multi-resolvent hierarchy to systematically derive the ETH smooth function, which governs energy correlations in isolated quantum systems. By expanding correlation corrections into an improvable series, it moves beyond phenomenological models. The resulting framework provides testable predictions regarding parity structure and spectral moment conservation.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a systematic, microscopic theory for the ETH smooth function $f_O( ar{E}, \omega)$, which describes the energy dependence of off-diagonal matrix elements in isolated quantum many-body systems approaching thermal equilibrium.
main_result: A multi-resolvent hierarchy is constructed that systematically organizes correlation corrections into an improvable expansion, revealing a parity structure and providing a unified theoretical framework for $f_{ji}^2$.
method: The authors employ recursive projection identities combined with a Diagonal Closure Approximation (DCA) to expand the ETH smooth function as a series of correlation levels ($g^{(r)}_{ji}$).
model_or_system: The analysis concerns isolated quantum many-body systems governed by a Hamiltonian $H = H_0 + V$, where $H_0$ splits into system (S) and bath (B) components. The theory is applied to calculate properties related to energy eigenstates $|\psi_nangle$.
key_observables: The ETH smooth function $f_{ji}( ar{E}, \omega)$, diagonal overlaps ($p_{\mu i}^n$), and correlation terms like $C_{jij}^{nmn}$.
important_parameters: Energy ($ ar{E}$), frequency ($\omega$), and the order of correlation expansion ($r$).
main_assumptions: The development relies on projector idempotency for deriving rigorous sum rules, and approximations are made by neglecting reduced correlations in certain steps.
figures_summary: Not specified (Notes focus on mathematical identities and structural theorems rather than figure descriptions).
paper_structure: The paper builds the theory through defining the problem using ETH concepts, developing the multi-resolvent hierarchy via projection identities, deriving key spectral sum rules, and finally analyzing the resulting parity structure of the correlation corrections.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, systematic tool to calculate thermalization properties beyond simple mean-field or single-channel approximations, which is crucial for understanding quantum chaos in complex many-body systems.
